title: Text-to-Image Diffusion Models are Zero-Shot Classifiers
role: An untrained readout of per-prompt denoising error on a shared noisy input; the no-training baseline a score-path encoder must beat, and a binding test protocol
reads: Squared error between the clean image (SD: VAE latent; Imagen: 64x64 pixels) and the model's x0 prediction from x_t at random t under each class prompt
trains: nothing trained for zero-shot results; appendix fits a 20-bucket linear softmax over timestep-binned errors (needs labels) and calibration on a held-out set
combines: argmin over classes of the Monte Carlo mean of exp(-7t)-weighted denoising error, all classes scored on the same t and x_t, paired t-test pruning at p < 2e-3
adding: not addressed; weighted denoising error is used only as a proxy for log p(x|y)
noise_and_seed: Shared noise across classes gives ~100x sample efficiency and pruning another 8-10x; accuracy varies <1% across seeds, +-0.7% Imagen across splits
timesteps: Low noise weighted most (exp(-7t)); Caltech101 Imagen 68.9% heuristic vs 56.1% SNR weighting, which over-weights the lowest noise where Imagen is inaccurate
unseen: no + attribute binding on 2-object CLEVR renders: Imagen Color|Shape 73%, SD 59%, CLIP 53% (chance 50); position binding at chance for all
headline: Binding accuracy Color|Shape 73% Imagen 64x64 and 59% SD v1.4 vs 53% CLIP ViT-L/14 (chance 50); Cue-Conflict shape accuracy 84.4% Imagen vs 68.7% ViT-22B
suggests: Contrast score paths of different captions on the same canvas and seed as hard negatives; the diffusion classifier is the free baseline for 'sum lands on joint' (inferred)
model: Imagen 64x64 base model; SD v1.4; CLIP ViT-L/14 as baseline
